transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I had to come here because I'm being watched and monitored constantly by people outside. They are tracking my every move, and I don't feel safe anywhere I go anymore. I just need to know how to make them stop.
I can hear how overwhelming and scary it must be to feel so unsafe right now. To help me understand how this stress is affecting your physical well-being, how has your sleep been lately?

I haven't really paid much attention to how I'm sleeping lately, so I'm not entirely sure. I'm just constantly on edge and trying to stay safe from the people who are watching me. It's really hard to focus on anything else when I feel this anxious all the time.

  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "mood",
  "question": "It sounds incredibly exhausting to carry that level of anxiety and tension every day. Aside from feeling anxious, have you noticed your mood feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless
I don't really feel down or hopeless, to be honest. My mood is more flat and empty, although I am constantly tense and on guard.

  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "mania",
  "question": "Thank you for clarifying that for me. Have you ever experienced periods where
I'm sorry, but it seems like you didn't finish your question. What kind of periods were you asking about?
My apologies for that. Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energized, hyperactive, or felt like you needed very little sleep for days at a time?

No, I have never experienced periods like that. I don't get bursts of high energy or feel hyperactive, and I've never felt like I could go without sleep. Mostly, I just feel very tired and constantly tense.
Have you ever heard voices, whispering, or other sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?
No, I have never heard any voices, whispering, or unusual sounds like that. Everything I hear is just the normal background noise of where I am.
How long has this been going on, meaning how long have you felt that you were being watched and tracked by these people?
This has been going on for about a year and a half now. I first noticed them tracking me about 1 year and 6 months ago, and it hasn't stopped since.
Apart from feeling anxious about being watched, how has this affected your ability to manage daily responsibilities, like working, keeping up with chores, or staying in touch with family and friends?

It has been really hard to manage anything, and I just don't have the motivation to do basic chores or work tasks anymore. I've also lost all interest in keeping in touch with my family and friends, so I mostly just stay isolated. Everything just feels like too much effort.

Sometimes when people are dealing with this level of constant stress, they find it hard to keep their thoughts organized or find that others have trouble following what they are saying. Have you noticed anything like that?

I haven't really noticed my thoughts being disorganized, but sometimes I feel like my mind just wanders off to completely different things. It can be hard to stay on one topic when I'm trying to explain what's happening. I don't think other people have mentioned having trouble following me, though.

You mentioned having a hard time with chores and feeling a lack of motivation. Have you also found it difficult to keep up with your personal self-care, like bathing, grooming, or changing your clothes?

Yes, I have found it very difficult to keep up with things like bathing, grooming, or changing my clothes. I just don't have the motivation or energy to initiate those tasks anymore. Most days, I just can't bring myself to do it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persecutory delusions of being watched and monitored for 1.5 years, accompanied by prominent negative symptoms including flat affect, avolition (lack of motivation for self-care, chores, and work), and asociality. The combination of delusions and negative symptoms, lasting over 6 months with marked functional decline, meets the criteria for Schizophrenia. Delusional Disorder is less likely due to the prominent negative symptoms and significant impairment in self-care and functioning, and mood disorders are ruled out due to the absence of depressive or manic episodes.
